paragraphs.text: The saints: those set apart for Christ, that is, the Christian believers.
God chose Paul to be His servant, as He declared to Ananias (Acts 9:15), and he sends this epistle to the Christians in Ephesus.

Paul sends his good wishes to the Church of Ephesus for the work of divine grace in them. This includes all the blessings, which he sums up in the peace that fills their hearts. They receive these blessings from the Father and the Son, which shows the equality of the hypostases together.
May you begin your words with others with wishes of blessing for them or words of praise, so that their hearts rejoice and they are thereby ready to hear the rest of what you say.

Blessed: worthy of praise and thanksgiving. The Father of our Lord: he speaks of the Father who created us and gave us all blessings, and of Christ His Son, who became incarnate for our redemption. So he speaks of the hypostases of the Father and the Son.

In heavenly places: the spiritual blessings that He gave to the heavenly ones and gives us a share of on earth. In Christ: we receive these blessings through Christ the Redeemer, and they include the Holy Sacraments and all the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church.
Paul begins his discourse by thanking God for the spiritual blessings that He granted to the believers in the Church.

Chosen us: by God's foreknowledge and love He knows who will believe in Christ, so before He created us He chose us in order to give us His blessings. This produces humility in us, because He is the cause of our blessing and not we ourselves. In Him: in Christ the Redeemer, in whom we will believe and receive salvation.
Before the foundation of the world: that is, in God's intention even before He created any human being, for He loves us and wants to bless us.
Holy: set apart for His love and for a life of holiness and righteousness with Him.
Without blame: without sin, so that we live in purity.
In love: the love of God, which created us, gives to us and helps us toward holiness.

St. Paul the Apostle makes clear a second reason for thanking God, namely His love, shown in choosing us before He created us, to be His children and to be sanctified in Him. The purpose of our existence in life is holiness and enjoying fellowship with God.
Predestinated us unto adoption: He chose us to become His beloved children.
By Jesus Christ: but the basis of this sonship is faith in His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ and the second birth of Baptism.

According to the good pleasure of His will: God rejoices in the sonship of His children, in their belonging to Him, their obedience and their blessing Him. God's aim in choosing us is not only to save us from our sins and the sentence of death, but that we become His children and so enjoy all the blessings of His fatherhood.

How great is the grace of sonship that God has given us! May we use it to draw near to Him and enjoy fellowship with Him, and at the same time keep away from the evils of the world by keeping His commandments and cutting off the causes of sin, however prevalent they are in the world or dear to us.

When we become children of God by adoption, this makes us praise Him, thank Him and extol His glorious grace, which He bestowed on us in honor of Christ. At the time of the baptism in the Jordan and at the time of the Transfiguration, "the Beloved" was the title by which the Father named Him: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 17:5). The Father loved the Son, and by our union with the Son we too have become beloved of the Father, and He has lavished His grace upon us.
Wisdom: right conduct at the right time.

Prudence: the skill of God. He accomplished redemption for us by the blood of Christ, and by this redemption we have the forgiveness of sins. This free redemption showed us the abundance of God's love, which flows from His countless treasures, and this grace also gave us wisdom and prudence generously.
Which He purposed in Himself: His desire to redeem mankind by giving Himself for it.

The wisdom and prudence with which God favored us made it possible for us to know God's purpose, which is the redemption of His people. This purpose was hidden in former times, but has now been made known by the favor of His grace and by the wisdom and prudence He gave us. This purpose and this justification came about without anyone's counsel.
The fullness of times: the time in which Christ became incarnate.

God ordered the times and seasons for the carrying out of His purpose, which is the accomplishment of the mystery of redemption, in order to gather together the believers, the members of the body of Christ. Christ is the head of all, and He is the head of the Church, and so that reconciliation might be accomplished by the blood of the Cross between those on earth and those in heaven.
In whom: that is, in Christ.
An inheritance: God gives us a portion in His Church through the Holy Sacraments and the work of the Holy Spirit in us.
Predestinated: by the ordering of God's eternal love for us.
Who works all things: God who works in all His children.
The counsel of His will: that is, His fatherhood, which ordered our salvation.

God has loved us from eternity and ordered our salvation in the fullness of time by the redemption on the Cross, and we receive this salvation in the Church by the grace of the Holy Spirit, through the Holy Sacraments and all spiritual things.
May we thank God every day for what we receive in our spiritual and bodily life, so that we feel the value of His gifts and enjoy them more and more.

entries.section: (4) The Holy Spirit for all believers

paragraphs.text: God gave us these gifts to be a means of praising and glorifying His majesty. "We" here refers to the Christian believers of Jewish origin, who had the promises and believed in the Christ promised in their Scriptures, for they had learned from the prophecies of the Old Testament to expect the coming of Christ.

entries.section: (4) The Holy Spirit for all believers

paragraphs.text: In whom: that is, in Christ.
You also: the believers from among the Gentiles.
The word of truth: the Gospel, with all the teachings it contains, is truth, and there is in it nothing of Jewish tradition or Greek philosophy; it is the truth that brought salvation.
Sealed: by your faith in Christ God has marked you as set apart for Him, and you received the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in you through the sacrament of the Holy Myron.

Paul addresses the Christians in Ephesus who were of Gentile origin and tells them that when they accepted the proclamation of the Gospel and believed it, they deserved to receive the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit in them.

entries.section: (4) The Holy Spirit for all believers

paragraphs.text: The earnest of our inheritance: an earnest is a part of the price paid in advance, and it points to the spiritual blessings that we receive in the Church, which are a sample of the glories and blessings that we will receive in heaven. The purchased possession: the believers in Christ whom He purchased with His blood.

Paul makes clear that what the believers receive in the Church of the Holy Spirit, in the form of the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace such as prayers and meditations on the Holy Bible, is the earnest of what we will receive in eternity. For these blessings that He gives to His people whom He purchased with His blood, that is, His Church, we thank Him and glorify Him for these gifts.

The Holy Spirit works in the Church and is ready to give you as much as you desire. In proportion to your attachment to the Church and your submission to the work of the Holy Spirit, you will enjoy Him, and even taste moments of spiritual feelings higher than the moments of this age, for they are a small light from eternity that you see on earth.

The saints: the believers. Paul heard of the faith of the Church of Ephesus and its love for all the believers, so he always gives thanks to God for the spiritual gifts He has bestowed on them, and prays, asking for all good things for them.

The God of our Lord Jesus: of course the Father is not God to the Son, since the two are one in essence. But the expression here means that Christ, in His incarnation and when He took on our humanity, became subject to the Father. Paul does not mean to diminish the divinity of the Lord Christ, since he himself said, "Great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh ... preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory" (1 Tim 3:16). The spirit of wisdom: that is, the Holy Spirit, who distinguishes all things.

The revelation in the knowledge of Him: that is, the disclosure of truths about God to the believing human being and the showing of His work in His creation. In this verse Paul brings together the three hypostases: the Father sent His Son in the form of weakness to redeem mankind and then raise it in Him to heavenly glory, and from Him proceeds the Holy Spirit, who binds the believers to God.
The eyes of your understanding being enlightened: you believe and see what human eyes do not see.
The hope of His calling: the hope in the Kingdom of Heaven which the Gospel proclaims.
The riches of the glory of His inheritance: the greatness of the eternal glories.
The saints: the believers.

The Apostle asks for the Christians in Ephesus that they believe the good news, so that they may see with the eye of faith the hope in eternity and its great glories, which God gives to all who believe in Him.

The Apostle shows how great is the power of the Holy Spirit working in the believers, and he expresses His power with the words "greatness ... exceeding ... mighty", to show the power of the Holy Spirit in supporting a person to leave his sins, to be joined to God, to love Him and to grow in knowing Him.

Without prayer and asking for God's help the human mind cannot understand the things of God. As the Fathers say, the one who does not love prayer has nothing good in him at all. May you hasten to God in all your needs, and even take care to praise Him and thank Him, so that your knowledge of Him and the longings of your love for Him increase.
His right hand: signifies the power and the complete glory that Christ received by His ascension into the heavens as a representative of the human race, to open the way for us.

The Apostle makes clear that God, by the power of His Holy Spirit, raised Christ, caused Him to ascend and glorified Him in the heavens, not to glorify the Son in Himself, for He is glorified from eternity with His Father, but as a perfect man. His resurrection signifies our resurrection from sin and encourages us, however far away we may be, for His Holy Spirit is able to draw us and raise us from our weaknesses and give us glories in heaven with Christ our Lord.

Not only in this world, but also in that which is to come: that is, not only the rulers and great ones we know in this life, but also what we may see in eternity, for Christ is above all. By Christ's ascension and sitting at the right hand of the Father, He was raised in His humanity above all the ranks of angels, whether "principality" or "power" or "might" or "dominion"; all the angelic orders have come under the authority of Christ. And not only all the ranks of angels, but also above every authority or power in the world of all creatures, in this world and the next.

Put all things under His feet: the full realization of which will take place in the final victory of Christ at His second coming (1 Cor 15:24, 25). By the glorification of Christ in His sitting on the heavenly throne He has become head over all things; He is on the throne of the headship of the universe and He is the head of the Church. He raised her to the highest place, and she has the right to sit on the throne with Him when she completes her striving. Thus He gave her authority over all earthly powers, so that if they plot against her, their plots come to nothing. Just as He made the angels serve her, He subjected the demons to her: "the gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (Mt 16:18).
The fullness: the Church is filled with the work of the Holy Spirit in her.
That filleth all in all: the Holy Spirit fills all the needs of the believer.
In all: all the believers.

The Church is the body of Christ, so she lives by His life and is glorified by His glory, and she is filled by the Holy Spirit, who fills all the needs in all the believers. He fills the whole Church because when the believers partake of the Body and Blood of Christ, He unites with all and fills them, and the Holy Spirit within them works in them to fill them at all times according to their response to Him.

God wants to fill you and satisfy you and even raise you above all the evils of the world. So know that you are not of this world, that you may leave your sins and separate yourself from all realms of evil to enjoy fellowship with Christ, looking to the Kingdom that awaits you.
Christ unites mankind in His Church
St. Paul the Apostle describes the state in which the pagan peoples and all the world were before faith, which is a state of spiritual death and separation from life with God.
Wherein: the trespasses and sins.
In time past: before faith in Christ.
The course of this world: the evil prevailing in the world.

The prince of the power of the air: the devil, who is a spirit and the chief of the demons that war against mankind and move in the air surrounding the earth. He is the chief of the evil spread in the air, and not the air itself, which God created.

The children of disobedience: those subject to evil, walking in it and far from faith in Christ. The Apostle makes clear that walking in trespasses and sins is according to the spirit of evil, that is, the devil, who is the chief of the powers of darkness that work and move in the air, that is, in the atmosphere surrounding the earth. He is the devil who suggests evil and sins in the minds of men, and he still works to this day in those who are still under his authority, and presents his sins to all people.
Among them ... even as others: they are the wicked people of the world, or the children of disobedience.

We Jews all, before we believed, walked like them, that is, like the rest of the wicked in the pagan world, before Christ rescued us. We walked according to our fleshly desires, driven by the lusts of the flesh and the evil thoughts that stir the passions. And because of the evil works that we did, we deserved divine wrath and eternal destruction.

The transforming grace of God has worked in us, so that we have become of a new nature. Therefore we must use all its possibilities to know God and enjoy fellowship with Him, and not slip into the sins we have left; and if we fall, we rise quickly and renew our mind in the sacrament of repentance and confession.
God is not merely merciful but rich in mercy, that is, abounding in mercy (Ps 51:1). And God is love, that is, there is in Him an unlimited love that moves Him toward us with mercy that has no end.

God's mercy was expressed in raising us from the spiritual death of sin, though we were not in a state of righteousness or holiness; rather, He loved us while we were His enemies. This is the wonderful divine love with which He loved us and which He showed us by the coming of His Son Jesus Christ in the flesh, His death for us on the Cross and His resurrection from the dead. By the power of Christ's resurrection God raised us from spiritual death, so our resurrection springs from His resurrection. The phrase "by grace ye are saved" is a summary of the work of divine love and mercy toward us. The Apostle tells the believers that they have obtained salvation from sin and resurrection from spiritual death by the grace of God, that is, by favor and kindness and not by merit.

God raised us with the resurrection of Christ, and just as Christ sat at the right hand of the Father in the heavenly places, He gave us to be at the right hand of God with Christ. This is by our union with Christ through Holy Communion, so that we have the right, if we abide in Him, to receive a place in the Kingdom. For Christ, by His resurrection, His ascension and His majesty in the heavens, is the representative and delegate of mankind. His resurrection and ascension are the resurrection and ascension of the human believers in Him when they hold fast to Him and the Holy Spirit works in them, until after this life He brings them to the Kingdom. This encourages us to rise from our sins and to hope for eternal life.

The grace of God is ready to work in you however great your weakness. Do not be troubled by the repetition of your sins or by your falling into a hard sin, for God's mercy is greater than all your sins, and He is ready to set you free from them however long they have enslaved you. Only persevere with faith in imitating God and in repentance, confident that He is able to raise you above all evil and even to give you the joy of fellowship with Him.
The exceeding riches of His grace: expresses the greatness of the work of grace, which surpasses the mind.

That in eternity there may be shown, and revealed to all creation and before the angels also, the greatness of His grace in the love of Christ the Redeemer and His longsuffering toward us until we repent, and His encouragement and support of us until at last He gives us salvation in eternity.
That: faith.

You have received salvation by the renewal of your nature in Baptism and your union with Christ in the Eucharist. All this is by the work of grace, but on condition of your faith in Christ; and this faith too is a gift and a grace from God, which you accept and respond to and hold fast in continual striving, and so enjoy all its blessings.
The salvation you have received is not the result of your works. God has saved you by grace, so that no one may find an occasion for boasting afterward.
His workmanship: He created us as human beings and then renewed our creation in the new birth by Baptism.

We Christians have been created a second time by Baptism, because we were dead in sin, and Christ raised us and gave us new life by Baptism. The purpose of the new nature is that we do good works of love and holiness and all the works of spiritual striving. These works were in the mind of God before He created and redeemed us, and He prepared them for us that we might walk in them and enjoy fellowship with Him through them. It is clear from this verse and the verse before it that salvation is by the blood of Christ and not by human works. But the grace that gives us salvation must produce good works that we do and strive in; otherwise the absence of good works confirms that we have not received grace and have not responded to it.
Made by hands: the circumcision of the Jews was nothing but an outward mark, because true circumcision is the circumcision of the heart.

St. Paul asks them to remember their state before faith. He tells them that they were pagans, uncircumcised, that is, the uncircumcised, and therefore outside God's shepherding of His people and God's covenant with them. The Jews called them "the uncircumcision", as a sign that they were not bound by a covenant with God.
Without Christ: that is, without hope or expectation of a Christ who would come so that they might obtain salvation through Him.

Aliens from the commonwealth of Israel: not of the chosen people of God who shepherds them, that is, Israel. Strangers from the covenants of promise: strangers to the essence of the promise, who is Christ the Redeemer (Acts 13:32). Having no hope: it is hope in salvation by Christ the Redeemer on earth and then complete salvation in the Kingdom.
Without God in the world: without knowledge of God or relationship with Him, for they separated themselves from Him by sin and by refusing to know Him.

He speaks to the people of Ephesus, who are Gentiles, that is, non-Jews, saying that before faith they had no hope in the awaited Christ the Redeemer and were far from knowing God and enjoying His care.
The blood of Christ: which gives us salvation through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace.

In the Old Testament the Jews were near to God by the sign of circumcision and the blood of the sacrifices offered to Him, while the Gentiles were far from Him. In the New Testament the believers, Jews and Gentiles, have become near to God through Baptism and Holy Communion, and members of His body, that is, the Church.

Our peace: He gave peace within the believer, so that there is no conflict between his body and his spirit, and peace among all the believers, Jews and Gentiles, for they have become members of one body.
Both: the body and the spirit, or the Jews and the Gentiles, or those on earth and those in heaven.

The middle wall of partition: which separates the Jews, as a people special to God, from the Gentiles who were far off, so that they became one people. This barrier is also sin, which separated man from God and made a division within man between his soul and his body.

There was enmity between the people of ancient Israel and the pagan peoples, and they did not mingle with the rest of the Gentiles, since the Jews regarded the Gentile as unclean, and it was forbidden for the Gentile to approach the temple; there was a high barrier separating the inner court from the court of the Gentiles. But in Christ Jesus all became one, and those on earth were reconciled with those in heaven, and He made both one, making peace for all with one another and between all and God.
The enmity: between the Jews and the Gentiles, and between God and man.

The ordinances: those which stood in the practices of the people of Israel, such as circumcision, the purifications and not eating certain animals. The Lord Jesus abolished them by His death on the Cross, because they were a type of His sacrifice. Christ, by accomplishing redemption, created one new man, neither Jew nor Gentile, and thus the Jews and the Gentiles become one man in Christ. They are no longer in enmity, but peace and love prevail among them, and they all become a cause of peace for those around them.
Having slain the enmity thereby: by the death of Christ He trampled and slew the death resulting from sin, and so removed the enmity between man and God and also between the Jews and the Gentiles.

By Christ's redemption on the Cross, He gave the Jews and the Gentiles who believed in Him a new nature, so they became one together and were also united with God and became His body, that is, the Church, since Christ removed the sin that was a barrier between Him and man.

Sin is the cause of division among people, so repentance is what opens the way for love between you and others. In proportion to the love you show to every person, you prove that you are a Christian and a member of His body, and so you live in peace within yourself and spread peace and love among people.
Them that were nigh: the Jews.
Them that were afar off: the Gentiles.
Christ came preaching peace, fulfilling the saying of Isaiah the prophet (Isa 57:19), and the Apostles preached in His name, proclaiming peace and forgiveness to all peoples, Jews and Gentiles.

Christ brought us near to God, we Jews and Gentiles (1 Pet 3:18), so we obtained reconciliation with God and became, through Him and by the work of the Holy Spirit, part of His people. Here the work of the Holy Trinity in reconciliation appears: "through Him (Christ ....) in one Spirit (the Holy Spirit) to the Father."
Strangers: means lodgers, that is, temporary guests.

The estrangement was removed from the Gentiles by the redemptive work of Christ, and they became, together with the Jews who believed in Christ, one people; indeed they became so near that he calls them the household of God.

The building on which our faith stands has as its foundation the apostolic teaching that we received from the Apostles and of which the prophets prophesied, and it is the guide for the teaching of the Church and her whole life. The subject of the preaching of the Apostles and the prophets is Jesus Christ the Savior, whom St. Paul the Apostle likens to the cornerstone that binds the two walls meeting at right angles, which signify the Jews and the Gentiles, so they became one people when they believed in Christ.

In Christ the chief cornerstone the believers in Him are united, so they are like stones fitted together and fixed on the foundation, the chief cornerstone, that is, Christ. Indeed this building grows, that is, is sanctified as the temple of God by His dwelling in each one by His Holy Spirit and His dwelling in His Church through the Holy Sacraments.

Here the Apostle speaks of the whole Church together, including the Gentiles in Ephesus and the churches of Asia, saying that she becomes a holy temple for the dwelling of God, as he also said in (1 Cor 6:19), "Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?"
May imitating the person of Christ be the basis of our conduct and our dealings, as He is the basis of our faith.
God's surpassing love in the salvation of the Gentiles

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: Because the door of faith was opened to the Gentiles and St. Paul the Apostle carried this call to them, he became a prisoner, imprisoned in Rome for the sake of Christ and for the sake of preaching to them.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: God declared His will to Paul by His divine dispensation twice: the first when Christ appeared to him in a great light on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:4-6), and the second when He appeared to him in the temple while he was praying, saying to him, "Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles" (Acts 22:6-21). In this dispensation we see God's wise plan to call the Gentiles to salvation.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: The mystery: the salvation of the Gentiles like the salvation of the Jews.

Here he refers to the earlier revelations that qualified him to be an apostle and made known to him what cannot be known except by revelation, namely that he should proclaim the Gospel among the Gentiles, as he had written before that the call is addressed to both Jews and Gentiles, and that both groups have become members of one Church, bound together by faith and love.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: As I wrote afore: what Paul wrote earlier, briefly, about Christ the Savior of the Gentiles.

When you read what came before in this epistle, you will be able to understand my deep knowledge of the mystery of Christ through divine revelation, and you will have gained understanding and enlightenment to grasp this mystery, which is the acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: In the generations before the coming of Christ the sons of men did not know of this mystery, which was revealed to Paul and to the rest of the Apostles and prophets in the New Testament after the descent of the Holy Spirit, although there are some hints in the Old Testament, such as "Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people" (Deut 32:43), "in him shall the Gentiles trust" (Rom 15:12, Isa 11:10).

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul the Apostle shows that the mystery of Christ is that the Gentiles share with the Jews in the blessings of the Kingdom of Christ, and that the Gentiles who became Christians are equal with the Jews who became Christians in the rights of spiritual inheritance and in being members of the body whose head is Christ, and that the promise of redemption, which was given to Adam and Eve and repeated to Abraham and the prophets of the Old Testament, has a share in it for the Gentiles just like the Jews. This is in Christ, that is, by union with Christ, which is the only condition for the Gentiles' sharing with the Jews in the blessings of redemption, and the Gospel is the means of their union with Christ.

God's love and arms are open to all people, that everyone who believes in Him and lives in His Church may be saved. So let your heart be open with love to everyone, however far away or however much he rejects God. Pray for him and offer him your love, for God is able to change him, even after a while.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: Whereof: the Gospel, that is, preaching to the Gentiles.

The ministry of the Gospel is the work that God appointed for him, and in the estimation of St. Paul the Apostle this commission is a great gift and a great blessing that God granted him. Thus it is not a favor from himself or because of any personal competence in him, but the divine gift gave him mighty power to preach the Gospel.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul the Apostle humbles himself and says that he was not worthy to be an apostle and that he was the least of all the believers in the early Church, yet this great grace was given to him, to preach among the Gentiles the riches of Christ, that is, His wisdom, His holiness and His accomplishing salvation for the sons of men. These are riches the human mind cannot imagine the greatness of or fully grasp the truth of, because the Jews did not imagine that there was salvation for the Gentiles who were far from God.

entries.section: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

paragraphs.text: The fellowship of the mystery which from the beginning of the world hath been hid: that is, the Gentiles' sharing with the Jews in salvation. This mystery was hidden in the heart of God and the prophets pointed to it, then it was revealed by Christ the Redeemer. In the Greek text of the Gospel it reads "the dispensation of the mystery" instead of "fellowship", and it means God's plan for the salvation of the Gentiles together with the Jews.

Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, was granted by the grace of God to enlighten the minds of all the sons of men and teach them that the salvation of Christ is shared by the Gentiles with the Jews. This was in the heart of God from eternity, and He declared it plainly in the New Testament by the incarnation of His only-begotten Son and His redemption of mankind.
Principalities and powers: some orders of angels.

The manifold wisdom of God: that is, the wisdom that ordered the salvation of the Jews by their holding to the Law and the commandments that speak of the Messiah, and the salvation of the Gentiles by repentance from their sins and faith in Christ. God's purpose in preaching the mystery of redemption to the Gentiles is to enlighten all people concerning that mystery, not only human beings but also the angels of heaven, who have authority and great standing, when they see this mystery fulfilled in the one Church, as they see the Gentiles having become members of the body of Christ. Thus God showed His wisdom by the incarnation of Christ and by guiding people to faith according to God's eternal plan, which was fulfilled by the incarnation of His Son, His death and His resurrection.
By Christ Jesus we have boldness to draw near to God, confident with assurance that He accepts us as His children by adoption, and that is by our faith in Christ and our union with Him.

Is it fitting that the angels rejoice at our salvation and we do not rejoice? ... You can enjoy this joy when you thank God every day for His salvation and His gifts to you, then strive for works of goodness and mercy, keeping away from sources of evil.

entries.section: (3) The Apostle's prayer to strengthen their faith

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle speaks from within his prison in Rome and says to the people of Ephesus: You should not be weakened because of the sufferings and tribulations I am now undergoing, whether imprisonment, beatings or insults, but we should rejoice in sufferings for the sake of preaching, for these sufferings have become glory for man after having been disgrace and shame.

entries.section: (3) The Apostle's prayer to strengthen their faith

paragraphs.text: So that the people of Ephesus may not be weakened, St. Paul the Apostle declares that he prays for them with all humility and fervor in petition, with prostration and contrition before God, who is the source of all life for all beings of every kind, whether these beings are angels of their various orders or the families of men everywhere on the face of the earth, of their various races.

entries.section: (3) The Apostle's prayer to strengthen their faith

paragraphs.text: Strengthened with might: the Holy Spirit supports you and establishes you.
The inner man: the human spirit.
The essential petition in Paul's prayer is that God glorify them and distinguish them from the rest of mankind by His generous giving, in the work of His Holy Spirit within them.

entries.section: (3) The Apostle's prayer to strengthen their faith

paragraphs.text: That Christ may dwell permanently in the heart, and where Christ dwells by His Spirit, spiritual life and divine knowledge arise. By faith we are assured of His presence, we accept Him, we trust His promises and we hold fast to Him for salvation.

Take care to pray for all those around you, especially when they are troubled or stumbling, and continue your prayers and tears and prostrations, even your fasts, for them, until God lifts from them the warfare of the devil and they overcome and rejoice.

entries.section: (4) The love and power of Christ

paragraphs.text: The breadth: the extent of love so as to include all the Gentiles on the face of the earth.
The length: all people in all ages until the end of the world.
The depth: love's lifting of people out of the depths of evil and corruption to give them the salvation of Christ. The height: raising people to heaven to enjoy eternal glory.
With the support of the Holy Spirit and the dwelling of Christ in you, you will be established in the love of God with the rest of the believers and you will comprehend the dimensions of this love.

entries.section: (4) The love and power of Christ

paragraphs.text: Which passeth knowledge: surpasses the grasp of the human mind.
The fullness of God: the perfection of God.
The love of Christ for us passes knowledge; as human beings we cannot grasp it fully, but the believers must advance little by little in comprehending the love of Christ as far as they are able.

entries.section: (4) The love and power of Christ

paragraphs.text: The power that worketh in us: the power of the Holy Spirit.

The Lord has done more than we ask or think; God's generosity is not confined to the limits of our requests or our notions of what we need. There is no limit to the abundance of blessings granted to those in whose hearts Christ dwells by His Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (4) The love and power of Christ

paragraphs.text: God is glorified in the Church, His bride, in whom that glory is manifested, and she in turn is glorified by Christ her head in all times and in eternity. Amen, that is, let what he has asked be fulfilled, and he calls on all the readers of the epistle to agree with him in that.

We have an open account with God to receive many blessings, which we must ask for and work for with all faith and patience, so that we deepen every day and grasp His love through prayer and thanksgiving, and likewise through loving others and striving for their salvation.
Renewal, Christian conduct and steadfastness in it

Paul calls the believers to hold fast to the commandments of God that he preached to them. He describes himself as a prisoner in the Lord because he is not distressed by prison but accepts it for the sake of Christ. And more than this, he feels joy that he suffers and is bound for His sake, and this joy leads him to hold fast to God's commandments, so that his heart is moved to call all the believers to hold fast with him to God's commandments.

Hold fast to God's commandments however hard your circumstances, like Paul's circumstances in prison. Do not seek excuses for yourself and so fall into sin, but ask for God's help and you will see Him before you supporting you, like Joseph who refused sin and endured being thrown into prison, and so was raised to the throne of Egypt.
Lowliness: a person feels he is less than everyone, yet by God's grace he lives and is distinguished as well. Meekness: quietness of heart.
Longsuffering: good listening and gentleness toward others, whatever their faults.
Christian conduct with others depends on humility, quietness of heart and longsuffering, so that a person is able in love to bear the faults of others.

Because the Holy Spirit has united the believers in the body of Christ, that is, the Church, we must preserve this unity by making peace with others as far as we can, giving up material things and some rights.

The Coptic Church, inspired by the Holy Spirit, placed this text at the beginning of the prayer of Prime in the Agpeya, so that when the believer repeats it and then goes out into life, he walks in it according to the Christian calling.

All the believers form the one body of Christ, and in the body of Christ the Holy Spirit is the giver of life to all the members, and all the believers have one hope, that to which God has called us, which is the hope of the second coming of Christ.

The head of this body is the Lord Christ, and He is one King over the hearts of all. We all confess faith in Jesus Christ as Redeemer, Lord and God, since we have entered by Baptism into one covenant with Christ and with one another, by our unity in the Church.
Of all: this one God and Father cares for all His creatures, even if they deny Him. Above all: that is, the possessor of authority and lordship over all His creation.
Through all: He works through all, and His fatherhood appears in their lives, so they glorify Him.

We believe in one God and not in many different gods like the pagan Gentiles, and we do not look on Him in a spirit of bondage and fear as Judaism looked on Him in the Old Testament, but, receiving the spirit of adoption, we call Him Father and trust in His care for us and His shepherding of us.

Thus unity is achieved among the Christian denominations and confessions if they are based on one faith, one Baptism and one creed. Let us all pray for this, so that all may return to the one faith and the one Church.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The unity of the Church does not prevent the gifts given to her members from being different. To each member a gift has been given, so that none of the members is left without a gift. The spiritual gifts are one in their origin, that is, their source, but varied in their forms, and the Lord Jesus has given to each one of the believers according to the measure or extent that He willed for him.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle quoted this verse from (Ps 68:18) and took it as a prophecy of the victory of Christ at His ascension after He accomplished redemption on the Cross.
Led captivity captive: Christ triumphed over death by His death and resurrection, and over him who has the power of death, that is, Satan.

The people whom Satan had taken captive and who lived in hell, Christ snatched from this enemy, set free and redeemed by His grace and made His people, so they became captives of Christ, as the Apostle said of himself that he was "the prisoner of the Lord" (v. 1). Gave gifts: Christ, the conqueror who takes the many spoils of His victories, is able to enrich His soldiers with many gifts of the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Christ descended into hell through the Cross and brought out the spirits of the believers of the Old Testament who were in the grip of the devil.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: That Christ ascended implies that He descended; that is, He who came down to earth and took our nature is the one who ascended to the highest possible place, above all beings, visible and invisible. We cannot grasp the loftiness of the exaltation to which God raised Him, that He might fill all with the fruits and gifts of the Holy Spirit ... This is the saving work of the Lord for the believers.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit, who was poured out on the day of Pentecost, granted varied gifts and different endowments to the believers, so He gave some to be:
Apostles: those whom Christ chose to preach to the whole creation.

Prophets: not only those who foretell the future, but prophecy in the New Testament means speaking about our future, which is eternal life, so the meaning of prophets is those who teach the spiritual life and prepare people for the Kingdom.

Evangelists: those who go about proclaiming the Gospel, like Philip (Acts 8). Pastors: those whom the Lord appoints to shepherd the congregations or local churches. Pastors can be teachers, whether bishops and priests or members of the Church.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: This variety of gifts achieves completeness of knowledge, holiness and love for the believers in the Church, for these gifts complete the ministry to the believers in the Church so that they grow in the love of Christ and in knowing Him.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: A perfect man: the Christian perfection that we are required to strive toward.

The measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ: our measure of perfection is Christ, so we strive toward Him to reach as much perfection as we can, not the absolute perfection of Christ. We do not compare ourselves with others, but our only highest example is Christ. We learn from all the saints, but our striving is toward Christ.

God's will is that we grow and go deeper in the knowledge of Christ until we come to the unity of the faith, so that we know the Lord Jesus with increasing knowledge, that He may be our only goal and the joy of our hearts. In this way the members of the Church and her shepherds join together for the success of the Lord's work without division among themselves.

God gives gifts to all His children in the Church, so try to know your abilities and gifts, and know that they were given to you so that you use them in the service of the Church. A gift is not a proof of your goodness, but using it faithfully increases your love toward God and benefits others, so God rejoices and blesses you.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: God does not want the believers to be like little children who have no stability or steadfastness, so that they are exposed to being deceived by the trickery and cunning of false teachers in order to achieve their malicious ends.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Let us stand firm in God's truth declared in His Gospel, confessing Him and loving Him, showing love to those who have strayed from Him, warning them gently and with a desire for the salvation of their souls, so that we reach spiritual maturity and grow in our spiritual life, imitating Christ the head of the Church.

Among the most important means that protect us from the misleading teachings proclaimed by some who have departed from the Church are studying the Holy Bible in a spirit of prayer and the interpretation of the Fathers of the Church. May we take care to read the Holy Bible every day and to attend the meetings and liturgies of the Church, and not accept teaching from anyone outside the Church, even if it seems dazzling.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: According to the effectual working in the measure of every part: every believer in the Church, whether his work is small or great, grows in the love of God, and by this growth, which sometimes seems small because this person's work is small, growth takes place for the whole body, that is, the Church.

The Church, composed of many believing members, is like the human body, composed of many members joined together and united. Every joint in it is a living member that contributes to the life of the whole body according to its function and its role in giving life to the body. The spiritual power that each member of the Church receives from Christ is a source of life for the whole Church, and the Church's growth in the likeness of Christ requires that she be full of love and all her members be united with Christ the Head and with one another.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle, who speaks by the Spirit of God, entreats the believers not to walk as the rest of the Gentiles walk, who walk in evil and defilement, led in that by their reprobate mind, deceived by evil.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The wretched souls far from God are separated from Him and have no spiritual life, because of the hardness and blindness of their hearts, and their minds are darkened because they are empty of God's light. And because their owners persist in evil, they are ignorant and refuse to know God.

entries.section: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The wicked Gentiles, whose consciences have died and no longer rebuke them for the evil of their deeds, commit unchaste sins without concern and without fear of God. Rather they go on in works of uncleanness and fornication with greediness and covetousness, and so they corrupt themselves.

Your knowledge of Christ, O believers, and of His principles and His life, and your experience of His power, which worked to renew your minds, this knowledge does not allow you to walk like the Gentiles in evil.

You have heard the voice of Christ, and hearing here is obedience of the heart and not merely hearing with the ear, and your hearing His voice requires of you not to walk like the Gentiles but by the commandments of Christ, that is, His truth.
The old man: the nature in man inclined to evil before Baptism, which dies in it, and man is born with a new nature inclined to good.
The Apostle calls the believers to reject their former evil works, in whose lusts they were immersed, and, instead of repenting, were filled with pride.
The spirit of your mind: the human spirit, which includes his mind and heart, and which the Holy Spirit renews.

The renewal of the believers takes place by their receiving the new nature in the sacrament of Baptism, and this renewal continues through the sacrament of repentance and confession. Renewal takes place first in thought, so that works become pure, befitting the children of God, and all this by the work of the Holy Spirit.
In Baptism we receive the new nature, which is inclined to be like God and to do good and righteousness and all works of holiness.

May you occupy your mind with prayer, spiritual reading and meditation, so that your life is changed by the power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in you, and you drive out the love of sin with the love of God's word and conversation with Him, and you incline to cling to the children of God and share with them in works of mercy.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: It befits the new man, created according to the will of God in righteousness and holiness, to be faithful and truthful in his works and in his words, and to leave lying so as not to deceive the other believers, because we are all members of one body, so none can deceive another without harming the whole body. Some may justify the sin of lying or divide it into kinds, but all of it is a great sin that keeps us from entering the Kingdom (Rev 21:8, Col 3:9).

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: Right anger is firmness for the good of the other and is joined with love, but in wrong anger a person loses his inner peace and it is accompanied by sins such as weak love toward others, even resentment, and it may appear in words painful to people or harmful actions. Paul continues his discourse, warning us that if we fall into wrong anger we should not continue in it, but forgive and reconcile with others before the sun goes down, that is, before the day ends, so that we regain our peace and the peace of those around us by apologizing and restoring understanding and love.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: If we keep some anger in our hearts, we thereby give the enemy of good an opening to enter our life and dominate it, so that he robs us of our joys, changes our relationship with people and fills us with malice.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: The Apostle warns the one who falls into the sin of stealing, through his selfishness, weak love for others and laziness, to rise and work with his hands, not only to meet his own needs but to turn to giving and meeting the needs of the needy. Thus we see Christianity transforming man from selfishness to giving.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: The warning here is against bad speech and the urging is toward good speech. The bad word is what stirs up unclean thought and leads to evil works, while good speech is what is beneficial to the hearers and contains teaching, advice and guidance, so that the content of the speech is according to the needs of the hearer, to give him spiritual benefit according to his need.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: The day of redemption: the second coming of Christ.

Evil conduct and bad words grieve the Spirit of God who dwells within the believers. This ought not to happen, because our members have been sealed by the Holy Spirit in the sacrament of the Holy Myron to be set apart for Him, and we live for righteousness until the end of our life, to receive salvation and the complete redemption of Christ when He brings us into the eternal Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: Bitterness: evil and distress within man.
Blasphemy: speech against God's commandments.

Let not harshness of character, which makes a person quick to anger, be among your qualities, and put away from you every inner feeling of distress, grumbling and discontent, which appears in the form of wrath, that is, intense anger full of cunning and evil and accompanied by clamor.

entries.section: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

paragraphs.text: Kindness is one of the fruits of the Holy Spirit, and our being kind to one another is a proof of our love. Our compassion and forgiveness toward others is a proof of our imitating Christ, for as God forgave us our sins and pardoned us and had compassion on us in the face of eternal destruction, so we must forgive our brethren.

Perhaps we think that if someone wrongs us he does not deserve our forgiveness. Do we then ask ourselves whether we were worthy of divine forgiveness?? ... However much someone wrongs you, he cannot reach the degree to which you have sinned against God, and yet He loved you and forgave you and all of us all our sins. Have you reviewed your attitude toward the one who has wronged you?!

Do not think about how much evil he has done, but about the measure of God's love for you in His forgiving you. Forgive the one who has wronged you for God's sake, and even pray for him, because sin is weakness and we are all liable to weakness, so support him with your prayers.
Christian conduct

entries.section: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks the people of Ephesus to imitate God in His love for us, because we are His children who love Him.

entries.section: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

paragraphs.text: Let us not have feelings of love only, but let them be turned into practical conduct in our love for one another, so that our love is self-giving, as Christ gave Himself for us in obedience to God the Father. For the sake of our love for God we sacrifice our lives in the service of others, counting our life the least thing we offer to God as a sacrifice of love, because of His surpassing love for us, so that our life rises as a sweet savor before Him and He rejoices in it.

entries.section: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

paragraphs.text: All uncleanness: all kinds of fornication and perversion.
Covetousness: love of money and possessions.
Let it not once be named: do not mention their names, and let none of the believers be characterized by them.

The Apostle forbids fornication of every kind, and likewise love of money and covetousness for the material things of the world. He does not want them spoken of among the holy believers, that is, those set apart for God, and no one is to be called by these evil sins.

entries.section: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

paragraphs.text: Filthiness: mocking talk about sexual matters.
Foolish talking and jesting: venting grumbling in words of mockery and trivialities.

The people of Ephesus were known for joking that included unclean talk and useless jesting, as a way of venting any distress they suffered. So the Apostle warns them to leave what they were known for, and even calls them to give thanks to God for His gifts that overwhelm them.

entries.section: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

paragraphs.text: An idolater: the fornicator makes lust his god and the covetous man makes money his god, so both are counted idolaters.
The Apostle warns us against evil lusts and love of money, whose end is eternal torment, so that we repent of them and leave them.

Your goal is love of God, which appears in love for all those around you, and by this you leave the love of sin and the lusts of this passing world. In proportion to the service you offer to those around you, you rescue yourself and keep it far from sin, since love for others takes the place of selfishness and satisfying the soul with the pleasures of sin.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: The Apostle warns the believers against what the pagans promote of ideas that match the pagan view of morals and conduct, namely that fornication and uncleanness are natural matters and do not defile the soul, while covetousness they regard as wisdom and not love of possession. The Apostle reinforces his warning against being deceived by those claims, because the wrath of God falls on those who commit these things, since they are rebels against God and disobey His commandments. So he forbids them to share in their sins and expose themselves to divine punishment.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: Darkness is a figure for ignorance and misery, and it is the state the believers were in before their faith and their accepting Christ as Redeemer and Savior; after their faith they became enlightened and a source of blessing and light to others. Christ is the Sun of Righteousness and His disciples reflect His light on others when they walk as befits the children of God.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: Goodness: works of good.
Righteousness: purity and justice.
Truth: honesty and uprightness.
God's purpose concerning us is that His same exalted attributes appear in us, for the new nature He gave us inclines to doing good and all that is upright.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: The children of the world seek what is pleasing to themselves, but the children of light make God's will the goal of every work they do or refrain from.

May we get used to asking ourselves before every deed: Does this deed of mine redound to the glory of the Lord? Is it what Christ wants from me? ... If I say this word or do this deed, shall I be fulfilling the will of my Master and Savior?

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: The works of darkness are those that the unbelieving person does because of the corruption of his heart and conscience, and they are unfruitful because they are of no benefit, indeed they are harmful to souls and expose them to eternal destruction. So the children of light must not share in them, and more than that, they should show by their words their disapproval of them, so that all may know how defiling and hideous they are.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: Those who commit evil works fear the light, so they do them in secret, and they are so shameful that even to mention them is also shameful. So we must refrain from mentioning them.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: All things: all the sins that are done in secret.
Whatsoever doth make manifest is light: every sin that we expose we are rid of, and our life is enlightened.

The Apostle shows the power of divine truth in the believers, because they rebuke the evils that the pagans do and so declare the truth, for Satan finds his opportunity in people's persisting in their evil when they hide their sins. But if a person faces himself, especially before spiritual people, the guilt of sin appears, so he repents of it and is enlightened by the light of God.

From here appears the importance of the sacrament of confession, when a person exposes his sins before his spiritual father, is rid of them and begins the struggle against them, especially when he is strengthened by partaking of the Holy Mysteries.

entries.section: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

paragraphs.text: St. Paul the Apostle quoted this verse from (Isa 60:1), and the quotation here is by meaning and not by wording. The call is to awake from the sleep of heedlessness and from the death of sin, for it is a call to repentance and spiritual wakefulness, and when a person rises from spiritual death by the life-giving power of Christ, Christ lights the way for him, so that afterward he lives and walks in the light and no longer walks in darkness.

Walking circumspectly means walking with care and spiritual alertness, paying attention to the snares Satan may set in our path to make us fall into them. We must know how to take each step, for the wise man is not deceived, while the fool goes through this world without reckoning the consequences of things.
Redeeming the time: means making use of the time available to us in this life, so we do not waste it on behalf of the world but use it in doing good.

The days are evil: what is meant is the multitude of trials and dangers that surround a person during his temporal life; therefore we must seize every available opportunity to lay up treasures for ourselves in the Kingdom of Heaven by holy worship and good works.
The Apostle calls us to use every opportunity for life with God because of the many wars of the devil that try to hinder us from it.

The door is open before us today to serve the Lord and work for the abiding life, before the door is shut and we are like the foolish virgins when the door was shut before them. May we make a plan at the beginning of each day so that we use our time in a better way, and also examine ourselves at the end of each day to repent of our sins and guard against falling into them in the days that follow.

Do not act foolishly and without wisdom, but you must understand the will of the Lord for His children, which is that you walk in holiness, as the Apostle himself says in (1 Thess 4:3), "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification."

The Apostle warns against drunkenness with wine because the spirit of drunkenness dominates the actions of the drunkard and his words, which are then marked by debauchery and rioting, things that do not befit the children of light, whose conduct must be controlled by the Spirit of truth, that is, the Spirit of God, who produces all the fruits of the godly Christian life.

Those filled with the Holy Spirit delight in speaking of God, who takes pleasure in His own, so they speak to one another of His love and His grace. Prayer and praise with God's word in the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs also helps toward being filled with the Spirit, provided that all of it is from the heart and not merely with the lips.
The name of our Lord Jesus Christ: in the name of Christ we receive salvation and all spiritual blessings, just as we close the Lord's Prayer with the words "through Christ Jesus our Lord."

Our thanksgiving to God is always for the bodily and spiritual mercies He has bestowed on us in our past life and until now. And thanks is for everything, even what may seem painful to us, because we know that all things in the end work together for good, so we thank God for all His gifts which we have received and receive through Christ the Redeemer.

Thanksgiving makes us feel that what we enjoy is from God, so we humble ourselves before Him, and this leads us to humility before one another so that we learn the virtues of others. God is before us, so we fear Him and are not proud and we reject all evil, and this drives us to greater humility toward one another, so we bear with them, give them precedence in honor over ourselves and learn from them all that is good.

After the Apostle called all the believers to be humble and submit to one another, men and women alike, because humility is the characteristic of all believers and a proof of their love for one another, he here specifies his words and calls women to submit to their husbands. For the personality of man, as God created him, inclines to leadership, bearing responsibility and giving of himself for those he is responsible for, and for this leadership to be carried out the wife must submit to him, because the family needs one leader and there cannot be two, or else conflict arises and leadership cannot be carried out. And because the Christian man leads his family in the fear of God, the wife's submission to him is submission to God. This submission does not mean not giving her opinion or sharing in making decisions, nor does it mean domination and control by the man; rather it is an ordering of the work and the taking of decisions within the family, and it suits the psychology of the woman, who wishes to have a strong man who leads the family and on whom she can lean.

Christian marriage is an image of the glorious relationship between Christ and His Church. Just as Christ is the head of the Church, which is His body, so the Christian husband is the head of the wife. And just as Christ cared for the salvation and peace of the Church, so the husband must care for his wife's well-being and happiness; for this reason this position was given to him, and not to dominate her or to be harsh in dealing with her.
So in the likeness of, and to the measure of, the Church's submission to Christ is the measure of submission due from the wife to the husband.

In every thing: that is, it is not permitted for the wife to submit in some things and not do so in others. But this obedience is to be in the Lord, that is, she must not violate God's commandments in obeying her husband's command.

The Apostle presents Christ's love for the Church as an example which he asks men to imitate in their love for their wives. Christ loved the Church to the point of giving Himself for her, and so a man ought to love his wife with this giving love.

The purpose for which Christ loved the Church and gave Himself for her is to sanctify her, consecrate her and set her apart for Himself, by cleansing her from the sins of everyone who joins her membership, with the washing of water, that is, by immersion in the water of Baptism, and also by the word, that is, by faith in Christ.
Spot: uncleanness.

Wrinkle: the corruption or alteration of a thing so that it is no longer good (like the creasing of a garment). By His redemption Christ gave salvation to His Church by renewing her nature through Baptism, and by this she regained her first glory in the garden of Eden and was rid of her evils and everything that corrupts her nature; indeed she became holy and set apart for life with Him. So the husband, by his love and self-giving, keeps every disturbance and evil away from his wife, and they live in one love with God.

Just as Christ, the head of the Church, gave Himself for the Church His body, so men should regard their wives as their bodies, that is, a part of themselves, so they love them and give everything for them. And by loving their wives they love themselves, because the two have become one. And just as no one is vexed with his body however many illnesses or pains it has, but takes care of it and attends to its needs, so the man must love his wife whatever faults or shortcomings she has, and even take care to complete and tend her, as Christ does with His Church.

As Christ nourishes His Church and brings her up, because she is His invisible body, the relation between Christ and His Church is like the relationship between Adam and Eve, for Eve was taken from the body of Adam and so is of his flesh and bone; likewise the wife is the body of the man, so he cares for it and tends it.

The Apostle quoted this verse from the Book of Genesis (Gen 2:24). The holy relationship between a man and his wife is closer than any other relationship, and the foundation on which each of the believers should build his relationship with his life partner is the permanent union between Christ and the Church.
The mystery: what the mind cannot reach to grasp.

What is meant by the mystery here is the union between the spouses, which is in the likeness of the union between Christ and the Church; it is not only one of the seven sacraments of the Church but also a deep union like the union of Christ with the Church.

The Apostle sums up the relationship of the spouses with one another: that the man love his wife as himself, and this is the first demand of all women, to be loved and always to hear expressions of love from their husbands. As for the woman's responsibility, it is to respect and esteem her husband, and this is the first demand of all men.

May every husband look on his wife as his church, so he loves her and gives his life for her as Christ did. And the wife looks on her husband as her Christ, so she loves him, submits to him and obeys him as the Church obeys the commandments of Christ.
Family commandments and spiritual weapons

entries.section: (1) A commandment for parents and children

paragraphs.text: The duty of children is submission and obedience to their parents. Among the sins that St. Paul the Apostle mentioned of the pagan Gentiles is that they were "disobedient to parents" (Rom 1:29-31). "In the Lord" means that the children's obedience to their parents is obedience to Christ, provided that this obedience does not violate the will and commandments of the Lord. The reason that St. Paul the Apostle gives is "for this is right", and the meaning of that is that disobedience is evil.

entries.section: (1) A commandment for parents and children

paragraphs.text: In ancient times God gave the Ten Commandments. The first four commandments were not joined with a promise, but the fifth commandment, concerning honoring parents, is the first commandment with promise: "that thy days may be long upon the land" (Ex 20:12).

entries.section: (1) A commandment for parents and children

paragraphs.text: The reward of honoring parents may be length of physical days on earth, or length and abundance of happy days in which a person enjoys the blessings of God, even though his life is short in days.

May children obey their parents and honor them, so that they enjoy God's blessings and this beautiful promise is fulfilled for them: "that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth." It is good to serve our parents, especially in their old age, in compensation for what they did for us.

entries.section: (1) A commandment for parents and children

paragraphs.text: Parents must beware of provoking their children by being harsh with them, for severe pressure on a young child causes him failure. So there must be love with firmness in dealing with children, along with disciplining them by making known to them the commandments of the Lord and bringing them up in a good religious upbringing.

May all parents sit often with their children and guide them well and know their hobbies and friends, and direct them to the teachings of the Holy Bible and to the Christian life. Every privilege is matched by a duty. Do we take care not to provoke our children, or do we only ask them to obey us??

The master according to the Spirit is Christ, while the master according to the flesh is the social position that existed at that time of masters and servants. So the Apostle commands servants that they ought to obey their masters with respect, obedience and great fear, and at the same time with pure hearts, not grumbling, full of love, as they feel toward Christ.
Eyeservice: is work done under observation.

Let the servants' service not be merely to please men, but let the servant do the work feeling that he is a servant of Christ Himself and offers the service to Christ and not as a slave to a man. In this way he is doing the will of God and carrying out His desire, expressing his love for Christ with all his heart.
Let the servants offer their bodily labor with good intention, counting the service and the toil as being for Christ and not for men.
Every good deed a person does, whether bond or free, he does not wait for his wages from men but receives his reward from the Lord.

The Apostle addresses the masters also, asking them to leave the manner of threatening in dealing with servants, warning them that they themselves are servants of a Master in heaven, who is Christ, who does not distinguish between one person and another because of his social position; with Him all are equal, and He judges among all with justice. By this he warns the believing masters so that they have the fear of the Lord. Thus Christianity raised the servants to the level of their masters, and afterward called for their liberation, so as not to cause social disorder had it begun by calling for the freeing of the slaves.

May you feel that you are dealing with God when you walk among people. Do not be troubled by insults, because God allowed them to correct your faults, and thank Him for every word of praise you hear from people, for it is encouragement from Him. And when you direct others, make sure that your words please God and are not from personal emotion. In this way you will feel God's presence with you, and He will bless your life.

We are weak in ourselves and our spiritual enemies, that is, the demons, are much stronger than we are, but by faith in the Lord and trust in Him we have sufficiency and the ability to overcome and be saved. However great the might of the enemy, Christ who is with us is stronger than he.

The devil our enemy does not war against us only in direct war, but uses many deceptions. So the Apostle asks us to prepare for him by putting on the spiritual weapons, which are complete, with no lack or gap, and include both defensive and offensive weapons, as we shall explain, so that we are able to stand against the enemy's attacks and even overcome him. And he says "put on", that is, the weapons are to be close to our bodies and cover us, so that it is no longer we who appear but Christ with whom we arm ourselves, and He is able of course to overcome the devil.
The darkness of this world: the evil prevalent in the world.
Spiritual wickedness in high places: that is, the demons were angels and fell, and their power is spiritual and not human, so it is loftier and stronger than the power of men.

The Apostle makes clear that our war is not easy because it is with the demons, who were angels of the orders of principalities and powers and rulers of the world, and fell. They have no authority except over the wicked, and because they are spirits their strength is greater than that of men, but when we arm ourselves with God we overcome them.
The whole armor of God: includes faith and all the practices of spiritual striving that the Church teaches us.
The evil day: the days of this life in which the devil attacks us with his evils.

Your nature is weak and the strength of your enemies is great, therefore take up the armor of God, for no other weapon can stand against the might of the enemies in the time of life in which we are exposed to temptation. And after you have armed yourselves with all the preparations and repelled all the attacks that come upon you, you remain firm, unshaken in the faith.
Stand before your enemies in the war. The girding of the loins above the waist is the first preparation for battle, and the girdle is Christ.

And the soldier's breastplate extends from the neck to the knee and protects the soldiers from the blow of the sword and the thrust of the arrow. What is meant here is that the perfect righteousness of Christ shields us from all external attacks, so we need only that our life be a life of practical righteousness, so that we give the enemy no entrance to the heart and conscience, by walking in the truth.
The Apostle calls us to walk by the word of the Holy Bible in our life, to protect us from every evil.

Shod: the soldier's boot is sometimes more important to him than the weapon in his hand, and without it he cannot move or run, especially on rough roads, for it protects him from thorns or slipping and falling.

The preparation of the gospel of peace: it is practical conduct in accordance with the teachings of the Gospel, such that our conduct is a living testimony to our peace with God, carrying the good news of grace and peace to souls far from Him. And the Gospel on which we depend enables us to pass through all difficulties, to tread on the thorns of the world and to climb over its rocks.

In addition to all the weapons mentioned we take up the shield: which was made of bronze, about a meter and a quarter long and three-quarters of a meter wide; the soldier fastens it to his left hand, and it protects the body from spears and arrows. And faith in the Christian struggle is like a shield, for by it we overcome the world and protect ourselves from its evils.

The helmet: a metal covering for the head that protects it from the enemy's weapons. The spiritual helmet is the helmet of salvation, that is, faith in Christ the Savior, who delivers our thoughts from evil and earthly things so that we think on heavenly things.

All the preceding weapons are for defense and protection, while the sword is for attack, and it is the soldier's tool for achieving victory and triumph over the enemies. What is meant by the sword here is the Holy Spirit, or the word of God which the Holy Spirit inspired in the writers of the divine books. There are no satanic devices that can shatter it and triumph over it. With the sword we cut off every sin within us, and it is double-edged, so it cuts off all kinds of sins.

May you always be ready, because the devil your enemy does not sleep. Hold fast to your faith and the word of God, taking care for your repentance every day, and you will be able to love everyone and seek peace with them, and so overcome the devil however great his power.
Supplication: is prayer for a particular matter.

To be strengthened in the Lord we must practice all the means of grace, among them prayer, since it keeps the Christian soldier in constant contact with the supreme Commander, the Lord Jesus Christ. We should pray at all times and not grow weary or be heedless. Our prayers will not be fervent and effective unless they are under the guidance of the Holy Spirit and His working in the heart. The believers are all one army, so the believer must not pray for himself only but for all the brethren also.
The mystery of the gospel: the salvation offered to all people, Gentiles and Jews, which the world did not know and the Jews did not believe.

He also asks them to pray for him, not that his chains be loosed and he be released from the prison in Rome, but that utterance be given to him, not in human wisdom but in the power of the Holy Spirit, when he preaches salvation to all people.

Although the Apostle was a prisoner in the prison of Rome and bound with chains, he counts himself an "ambassador" of the Gospel. While earthly ambassadors boast of the decorations they receive, the Apostle boasts of heavenly decorations, which are the chains with which he was bound. So he asks for their prayers that he may continue to proclaim the good news of Christ.

God will not look at the worldly honor we have received but at the faithfulness, godliness and conduct we have shown during our temporal life, and the sufferings, tribulations and trials we have borne with contentment and thanksgiving.

entries.section: (5) The Apostle reassures the people of Ephesus and greets them

paragraphs.text: Because Paul was imprisoned in Rome, the believers in Ephesus were anxious about him, so he sent to them Tychicus, his disciple, to reassure them about his words.

entries.section: (5) The Apostle reassures the people of Ephesus and greets them

paragraphs.text: As the Apostle sensed the longing of the believers for him and their desire to know his circumstances, he sent this epistle with Tychicus to comfort their hearts, and it was indeed a beautiful comfort in the truths and heavenly revelations it contained.

We should care about the feelings of others and take their concerns into account and not ignore them. So get used to offering words of encouragement and praise, and also to caring for those who worry about you, reassuring them even with a small word.

entries.section: (5) The Apostle reassures the people of Ephesus and greets them

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul sends peace to the believers who commit their lives to the care of the blessed Father, and he asks God the Father and His Son Jesus Christ, the source of spiritual blessing, to fill their hearts with love in addition to the faith they have.

entries.section: (5) The Apostle reassures the people of Ephesus and greets them

paragraphs.text: He closed the epistle with the apostolic blessing, in which he asks the grace of Christ for those who love Him and show this love by a pure life and walking in holiness.
